findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Disambiguate AC-3: state whether the invariant counts Agent CONSTRUCTIONS (native+prompted = 2) or agent.run_sync CALLS, and specify that the 895c-downgrade fixture presents a well-formed FIRST prompted response so no output-repair retry inflates the run_sync count (or restate the bound as '<= output_retries+1 run_sync on the prompted Agent').
evidence: AC-3: 'a test asserting one `agent.run_sync` on the happy path and exactly two (native then prompted) on the 895c downgrade, never a third'
structured_run.py:157-163 — prompted path builds one Agent then loops `for _ in range(output_retries + 1): ... agent.run_sync(...)`
structured_run.py:130 — native path's single `agent.run_sync` before the 895c fall-through

AC-3 also says 'constructs EXACTLY ONE outer Agent run' and 'the ONLY sanctioned second outer Agent run is the ... downgrade' — 'outer Agent run' = Agent construction, but the test clause counts `agent.run_sync`, a different quantity
findings.finding: AC-3's outer-Agent-run test assertion conflates 'outer Agent run' (Agent construction count) with agent.run_sync call count, leaving the counter placement for the 895c downgrade fixture ambiguous. In structured_run.py the PROMPTED path constructs ONE Agent (line 157) then calls agent.run_sync in a loop of output_retries+1 iterations (lines 161-163). On the 895c downgrade the native path makes 1 run_sync (line 130) and the prompted path makes 1..output_retries+1 more, so 'exactly two agent.run_sync ... never a third' holds only if BOTH the native downgrade fires AND the first prompted response validates without an output-repair retry. The AC does not state that the downgrade fixture must present a well-formed first prompted response, so a test author cannot tell whether the invariant counts Agent constructions (native+prompted = 2) or run_sync calls (2 only under the extra precondition).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC-3 / Testing 'AC-3 invariant' bullet
scenarios: 895c downgrade fixture whose first PROMPTED response is a parse/validation near-miss (not truncation) triggers an output-repair retry, producing a third agent.run_sync and failing an assertion that literally forbids a third
Test author counts Agent constructions (2) vs run_sync calls (2-or-more) and implements the invariant two incompatible ways
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC-3's test clause to: 'exactly one Agent constructed on the happy path (one agent.run_sync); on the 895c downgrade exactly two Agents constructed (native then prompted), with the downgrade fixture's first prompted response well-formed so exactly two agent.run_sync total — never a third Agent construction.'
